title: Chapter 3.  Geography — Valleys, Plateaus, Passes & Glaciers

blocks.content: Beyond the mountain ranges themselves, J&K's valleys and mountain passes are individually significant enough to be tested by name - this chapter catalogues the most important ones, along with the region's glacier systems.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Kashmir Valley lies between the Great Himalayas and the Pir Panjal Range.
Strategic Himalayan mountain passes enable vital connectivity across high-altitude border regions.
Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram Range is the longest glacier in the Indian subcontinent.
Highland plateaus like Ladakh and Deccan form essential physiographic divisions of India.

blocks.content: The Kashmir Valley (also called the Vale of Kashmir) is the geographic and cultural heart of the Kashmir division - an oval, bowl-shaped intermontane valley roughly 135 km long and 32 km wide, lying between the Pir Panjal Range (south/west) and the Great Himalayan/Zanskar Range (north/east), at an average elevation of about 1,600 m.

Geologically, the Valley is believed to have once been the bed of a large lake, whose gradual draining left behind the fertile, terraced plateau deposits known as 'karewas' (locally 'wudar'), extensively used today for saffron cultivation, orchards and other high-value agriculture.

The Valley is drained by the Jhelum River, which flows through it in a distinctively slow, meandering course before entering a gorge near Baramulla and exiting towards Pakistan-administered territory.

★ EXAM POINT: 'Karewa' land formations (ancient lake-bed terraces) are a distinctive Kashmir Valley geomorphological feature, famous for saffron cultivation, particularly around Pampore - a frequently tested geography-cum-economy crossover fact (see also Chapter 18, Economy).

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Note the functional overlap: several of these passes (Banihal, Pir Panjal, Sinthan) all connect the JAMMU and KASHMIR divisions to each other, while Zoji La uniquely connects the KASHMIR division to LADAKH - a distinction commonly tested when questions ask 'which pass connects X to Y'.

items: Zoji La Pass connects Srinagar to Leh and is frequently tested in geography sections.
Nathu La Pass is located in Sikkim and connects India with the Tibet Autonomous Region.
Siachen Glacier is situated in the Karakoram Range and is the world's highest battlefield.
Rohtang Pass connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys in Himachal Pradesh.

Kolahoi Glacier - the largest glacier of the Kashmir Valley proper, located in the Great Himalayan/Zanskar Range near Sonamarg/Pahalgam, and the principal source of the Lidder River; it has been observed to be retreating in recent decades, a subject of ongoing glaciological and climate-change research.
Thajiwas Glacier - a smaller, more easily accessible glacier near Sonamarg, popular as a tourist attraction rather than a major hydrological feature.
Machoi Glacier - located near the Zoji La Pass, feeding into both the Sind River (Kashmir side) and, on the other side of the pass, contributing to Ladakh's drainage.

While the largest and most strategically significant glaciers of the wider region (such as Siachen) lie within Ladakh UT rather than J&K proper, the Kashmir Valley's own glacier systems remain critical to sustaining its rivers, particularly during the pre-monsoon and dry-season months.
Kashmir Valley: bowl-shaped, ~135 km x 32 km, average elevation ~1,600 m, drained by the Jhelum; famous 'karewa' terraces used for saffron cultivation.
Key valleys: Lolab, Gurez, Sind, Lidder (Kashmir division); Chenab, Poonch/Rajouri valleys (Jammu division).
Key passes: Banihal (Jammu-Kashmir), Zoji La (Kashmir-Ladakh), Pir Panjal Pass/Mughal Road (Jammu-Kashmir), Sinthan Top (Kashmir-Kishtwar).
Kolahoi Glacier = largest glacier of the Kashmir Valley proper, source of the Lidder River; observed to be retreating.
Siachen Glacier (world's highest battlefield) lies in Ladakh UT, not J&K proper - but is frequently studied alongside J&K's Himalayan geography given the shared former-princely-state context.
